tagline: Electrolytes for a climate that takes them seriously.
description: Training in Kuwait means sweating at rates that a temperate-climate label was never designed for. We weight sodium content higher here than any other market would, and we reject the flavoured-water products that sell on packaging alone.

copy.unit_basis: Per serving. The types on this page do not share one comparison unit, so each product names its own.
copy.guide_heading: How do you like your hydration?

milk_allergy_empty.title: Nothing here is free of milk.
milk_allergy_empty.body: Every product published in this category declares milk. We will not recommend one against a declared milk allergy, and we do not pad the shelf with something we have not judged.

director_selection.note: Products a founder put on the shelf from the database, whatever their score.

types.name: Electrolytes
types.purpose: Sodium, potassium and magnesium replacement — which in Kuwait is not optional.
non_negotiables: Sodium at or above 300 mg per serving; anything less is flavoured water
Added sugar disclosed and under 6 g, or none at all
types.shelf_note: Kuwait summers make this the most consequential shelf on the site. We weight sodium content harder here than we would in a temperate market.

types.name: Intra-Workout Carbohydrate
types.purpose: Fast fuel for sessions past the ninety-minute mark.
